Why do most Ladner houses have crawlspaces or slab foundations instead of basements?

Ladner sits on low-lying Fraser River delta soils with a high water table. Municipal Flood Construction Levels (FCL) and geotechnical standards favour slab-on-grade or raised crawlspace foundations rather than deep below-grade basements.
Can a Ladner home under $1.8M have a legal secondary suite?

Yes. Many two-storey and split-level homes in Ladner contain ground-level 1- or 2-bedroom secondary suites that comply with City of Delta flood-construction elevation and building-code fire-separation rules.
What lot sizes are typical for Ladner homes under $1.8M?

Standard 1970s and 1980s subdivisions in Hawthorne, Holly, and Delta Manor feature 60-by-100-foot to 66-by-120-foot lots (6,000 to 7,920 sq ft), while newer compact infill single-family lots near Ladner Village or Port Guichon measure 33 to 45 feet wide.
Which schools serve Ladner's detached residential neighbourhoods?

All public elementary catchments in Ladner — Ladner Elementary (including French Immersion), Hawthorne Elementary, Holly Elementary, Port Guichon Elementary, and Neilson Grove Elementary — feed into Delta Secondary School (DSS) in central Ladner.
What should a home inspection focus on for 1970s–1980s Ladner houses?

Inspectors in Ladner pay close attention to crawlspace moisture barriers, perimeter drain tile flow, original poly-B or copper domestic water piping, electrical panel capacity, roof age, and any settlement in slab-on-grade garage or patio areas.
